findings.claim: The stats-backup importer rebuilds every imported day with TierResult(bronze:silver:gold:flawless:onTime:moves:elapsed:) and never passes `runs`, so the newly-added per-day clear log is silently discarded on import. On the feature's primary use case — restoring onto a new device — every solved day comes back with runs == [], and the new day card reports 'Cleared · best 96 moves in 5:41 · par 72' instead of 'Cleared 4x ... Moves each run: ...', permanently losing the history the backup file actually contained.
evidence: ios/Causeway/Causeway/Views/DailyView.swift:467-474
ios/Causeway/Causeway/Model/Daily.swift:346 (TierResult.runs defaults to [])
ios/Causeway/Causeway/Model/DailyStore.swift:33-38 (merge -> mergeTiers(local, imported); mergeRuns([], local) keeps only local)
ios/Causeway/Causeway/Views/DailyView.swift:1547-1554 (clearsSummary keys the count off r.runs.count)
findings.note: StatsBackup encodes/decodes runs correctly (TierResult is Codable); only the sanitising re-construction at the import site drops it. Fix is one argument: runs: r.runs (optionally filtered to rows with moves > 0).

findings.claim: The assertion that is supposed to prove auto-play refuses every tier-breaking send is a tautology: `refusals` and `unguardedBreaks` are both incremented inside the same `if (violated(after))` statement, so `assert.equal(refusals, unguardedBreaks)` can never fail for any implementation. The test named 'the look-ahead must refuse it' exercises no look-ahead code at all — it recomputes split-at's violation rule inline and compares it to itself.
evidence: tests/autofinish-tiers.test.mjs:150 (let refusals = 0, unguardedBreaks = 0)
tests/autofinish-tiers.test.mjs:161 (if (violated(after)) { unguardedBreaks++; refusals++; })
tests/autofinish-tiers.test.mjs:166 (assert.equal(refusals, unguardedBreaks, 'every breaking send must be refused'))
findings.note: The only surviving real assertion in that test is unguardedBreaks > 0, i.e. 'the repro still exists'. Nothing checks that any shipped autoSendWouldBreakTier declines it.

findings.claim: MUTATION-PROVEN: deleting `if(sent) continue;` from simulateAutoFinish — the exact edit the diff says is 'what lets prediction and execution agree card-for-card', because a different order predicts a different SPLIT — survives the entire node suite (120 tests still pass), including the 'canon: days 21, 24, 27' test and the 21k-position differential test. The differential oracle only compares `won`, which the file itself documents as order-independent, so no test constrains the predicted send order that autoFinishTierCost's split prediction is built on. A future reorder of the cascade would ship a Finish-cost dialog that names the wrong tiers with a green suite.

findings.claim: MUTATION-PROVEN: the rewritten fail-fast checker objViolated has zero behavioural coverage in either shipped copy. Mutating index.html's `case 'moves'` and `case 'end-bias'` bodies to `return false`, and iOS Daily.swift's `case "end-bias"` body to `return false`, all SURVIVE the full node suite. That is the same blind spot that let this function sit on a dead pre-parameterised id set ('aces-first', 'split-even', 'cells-le-1') for months with every objective falling through to `default: false` — the very regression this diff fixes. Only tests/daily.mjs's new canonical copy is tested (and only for end-bias and split-at); no parity test compares the shipped copies to it.

findings.claim: MUTATION-PROVEN: both web halves of bug/WF-4 can be neutered without any test noticing. Replacing `const sLive=!objViolated(ch.silver,base), gLive=!objViolated(ch.gold,base);` with `const sLive=false, gLive=false;` in autoSendWouldBreakTier (index.html:698) and in autoFinishTierCost (index.html:991) both SURVIVE the full node suite. findings.claim: The 'never forfeit the same-day grace silently' guard is gated on hasLiveGame, which requires moveCount > 0. A challenge started on day D with zero moves made (open the sheet, tap Play, background the app) restores on D+1 with challengeDay=D, challengeStartDay=D and moveCount=0, so graceLive is true but hasLiveGame is false: New game / Replay / Deal-Play reset with no dialog, restartDeal re-stamps challengeStartDay to D+1, and day D can never earn the on-time award again. Both platforms.
evidence: ios/Causeway/Causeway/Model/Game.swift:432 (hasLiveGame requires moveCount > 0)
ios/Causeway/Causeway/Views/ContentView.swift:343 (requestReset gates the whole confirmation on hasLiveGame)
ios/Causeway/Causeway/Model/Game.swift:258 (challengeStartDay is persisted, so a 0-move attempt survives relaunch)
index.html:1841 (hasLiveGame) and index.html:1849 (confirmReset returns true immediately when !hasLiveGame())
findings.note: Fix: OR graceLive into the gate (`hasLiveGame || graceLive`) so the grace dialog can fire at move 0.

findings.claim: Two of the three calendar tripwires call XCTSkipUnless on the very locator the fix introduces, so removing the fix turns the test GREEN (skipped) rather than red. Deleting the `.accessibilityLabel(locked ? "...locked until that date" : ...)` added in this diff makes the locked-cell query find nothing and testTappingALockedFutureDayExplainsWhy skips; likewise the Play-names-the-day test skips whenever the cell-label query returns nothing. A regression tripwire that reports 'skipped' on the regression is not a tripwire.
